findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
findings.body: When evt.destinationCalendar is null/undefined or an empty array, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError. Previously this was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which safely treated a missing calendar as not Google Calendar and fell back to Cal Video. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar now fails in EventManager.create instead of falling back.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of organization slug assignment
findings.body: This changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to set `slug` only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. That inverts the previous behavior: with team billing enabled the slug should be deferred as `requestedSlug` in metadata until billing is set up, and without billing the slug should be set directly. Organizations created with billing enabled will now get a slug immediately, and organizations created without billing will be created with no slug. This change is unrelated to destinationCalendar.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback to destination calendar is broken
findings.body: In updateEvent (and the same pattern in deleteEvent at line 315), the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and selectedCalendar/calendarId becomes undefined. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates/deletes called without an externalCalendarId (e.g. older booking references) will now call Google with an undefined calendarId instead of the booking's destination calendar.

findings.title: Credential from previous calendar reference is reused for next reference
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, `credential` is declared outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop. If a later reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup fails or returns an app without a slug, `credential` is never reset and still holds the previous host's credential, so `updateEvent(credential, ...)` at line 542 updates the wrong host's calendar (or updates the same calendar twice with another reference's uid). Each iteration must start with credential undefined.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Booking references for dedicated video integrations will now be persisted with credentialId undefined, so later update/delete/reschedule flows that look up the specific video credential by reference.credentialId cannot find it and may fall back to a wrong credential or fail to update/delete the meeting.

findings.title: Organizer email always taken from first host for every host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent correctly selects the target calendar by matching credentialId (lines 147-149), but the organizer attendee email is taken from mainHostDestinationCalendar (the first destinationCalendar entry) regardless of which credential/calendar is being written to. For a collective event, creating the event on the second host's Google calendar sends the first host's calendar externalId as the organizer email, which does not belong to that account and can cause Google to reject the insert or attribute the event to the wrong organizer. The entry matching credentialId should be used here, as it already is for selectedCalendar.

findings.title: Office365 (and other non-Google services) ignore credentialId and always use first destination calendar
findings.body: The Calendar interface now passes credentialId to createEvent so each destination calendar can be matched to its credential, but Office365CalendarService.createEvent still destructures only the first entry of event.destinationCalendar and builds `/me/calendars/{firstExternalId}/events` with whichever credential EventManager is iterating. For collective events the second host's event is attempted against the first host's calendar id using the second host's token, producing 404/duplicates rather than an event on the second host's calendar. The same first-entry pattern remains in LarkCalendarService.createEvent and BaseCalendarService.createEvent, so the multi-host fix only works for Google Calendar.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar, and the collective handling then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining on null this silently does nothing, so team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and those hosts receive no calendar event — exactly the collective case this PR aims to fix when only the non-organizer hosts have calendars connected.

findings.title: destinationCalendar shape change breaks webhook payload contract
findings.body: Changing CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` changes the JSON sent to webhook subscribers (evt is spread into sendPayload) from an object/null to an array, and call sites are inconsistent — some now emit [] (confirm, cancel, payment webhooks) while handleNewBooking can still emit null. External webhook consumers expecting an object will break, and consumers cannot rely on a single shape. This needs to be kept consistent (always an array) and treated as a breaking payload change, or the webhook payload should retain the old field shape.
